titulo: There is, and it is located
intro: Learn the distinction between hay (existence or availability) and está (locating a specific item).
b1.titulo: Existence and location: hay vs. está
b1.texto:
Use **hay** to state that something exists or is available, often with indefinite articles: *Hay una farmacia aquí*, *Hay dos bancos*.

Use **está** to pinpoint the location of a specific, known person or object: *La farmacia está al lado del banco*.

**Hay** remains unchanged for singular and plural nouns.

With **al lado de**, de + el obligatorily contracts to **del**: *al lado del banco*.
b2.f1.texto: There is a pharmacy in the square.
b2.f3.texto: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
b4.e0.texto: There is a pharmacy in the square.
b4.e1.texto: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
b5.f0.texto: In the historic centre of the city there is a beautiful square.
b5.f1.texto: Many calm neighbours walk around the fountain.
b5.f2.texto: There are several big trees and a small pharmacy.
b5.f3.texto: The main bank is next to the green park.
b5.f4.texto: The modern pharmacy is always open to the public.
b5.f5.texto: The customers buy medicine very calmly.
b6.o0: El museo está en la plaza
b6.o1: Hay un museo en la plaza
b6.o2: El museo es en la plaza
b8.frase: La farmacia está al lado del banco.
b4.texto:
Compare:
- **Hay** una farmacia en la plaza (states that one exists).
- La farmacia **está** al lado del banco (locates that specific pharmacy).
b6.pregunta: Which sentence locates a specific, known museum?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: use the definite article and estar to locate a specific building.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «hay un museo» states existence in general.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: ser is not used for the physical location of buildings.
b7.pregunta: Complete to state that a pharmacy exists.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: use «hay» to introduce an indefinite item that exists.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «está» requires a specific, determined subject.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «es» serves to define or classify, not to express existence.
b8.traduccion: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «There is a bank here».
p.hay.consejo: Impersonal form of haber stating existence or availability.
p.está.consejo: Third person singular of estar locating a specific subject.
p.la farmacia.consejo: Shop where medical prescriptions and drugs are dispensed.
p.la plaza.consejo: Open public square in a town or city.
p.del.consejo: Mandatory contraction of preposition de and masculine article el.
p.aquí.consejo: Adverb denoting the location close to the speaker.
p.cerca.consejo: Adverb of place indicating short distance.
p.farmacia.consejo: Where English has «ph», Spanish writes «f». And «c» before «i» sounds like «th»: far-MA-thya.
p.banco.consejo: «Banco» also means a bench to sit on. The context tells you which: «el banco de la plaza» is a bench.
p.plaza.consejo: In Spain the «z» sounds like «th»: PLA-tha. A «plaza» is the open square of a town.
p.hermosa.consejo: The «h» is silent, so «hermosa» sounds like «ermosa». It is a more elegant word than «bonita».
p.tranquilos.consejo: In «qui» the «u» is silent: tran-KI-los. Same family as «tranquilidad», peace.
p.alrededor.consejo: It is written as one word. After the «l» the «r» is strong: al-rre-de-DOR. It is often followed by «de».
p.principal.consejo: It has one form for both genders: «banco principal», «calle principal». The «c» before «i» sounds «th».
p.parque.consejo: In «que» the «u» is silent, so it sounds PAR-ke. It follows the same pattern as «queso».
p.moderna.consejo: It is the feminine of «moderno», to agree with «farmacia». Compare it with the English «modern».
p.abierta.consejo: Feminine of «abierto», from «abrir», to open. The «ie» glides into one syllable: a-BYER-ta.
p.compran.consejo: From «comprar». The ending «-an» is for «ellos» or «ellas»: «compran», «hablan», «cantan».
p.medicinas.consejo: It looks like English «medicine», but the «c» before «i» sounds «th»: me-di-THI-nas. Singular: «medicina».
p.histórico.consejo: Related to «historia»: «histórico» takes an accent on «ó», and the «h» is silent.
